catalog_quote: In Motuna, every vowel or consonant in rhyme position constitutues one mora. That is, every vowel or C2 consonant constitutes one mora. ... First, stress generally falls on the third mora from the last in the case of words consisting of three or more moras, and on the first mora in the case of words consisting of two moras, if such a mora is a vowel or an archinasal. If such a mora happens to be /Q/ or /H/, stress falls on the preceding vowel. cf. §2.5. ... 2.5 STRESS. Stress is predictable, and thus is not phonemic in Motuna. (1) Most words consisting of three or more moras are pronounced with a relatively level high pitch from the beginning till the third mora from the last, which is immediately followed by another mora showing significantly steep drop in pitch. ... tone_statements.citation: 大西正幸 [Onishi, Masayuki]. 2010. モトゥナ語におけるCi/Cu音節の短縮化 [Reduction of Ci/Cu syllables in Motuna]. 地球研言語記述論集 (RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series) 2: 165-194. Kyoto: 総合地球環境学研究所 (Research Institute for Humanity and Nature), Indus Project. Volume ISBN 978-4-902325-51-5.
tone_statements.quote: 2.2 モーラ モトゥナ語はモーラ言語である。少なくとも次の 3 つの点で、モーラは重要な役割を果たす。(A) 音韻語の最小単位は 2 モーラである。 … (B) ピッチアクセントが語末から数えて 3 モーラ目にある（3 モーラ目から 2 モーラ目にかけてピッチが急激に下降する）。下の例を参照。(4) a. miı́nong 「私（男）は行くところだ」 b. mı́ina 「私（女）は行くところだ」 (5) a. hónna 「大きい」 b. pońnaa 「多い」 (C) 部分重複は、もとの語の最初の 2 モーラを前接する。
tone_statements.translation: 2.2 Mora. Motuna is a mora language. The mora plays an important role in at least the following three respects. (A) The minimal phonological word is two moras. ... (B) The pitch accent is on the third mora counting from the end of the word (the pitch falls sharply from the third mora to the second mora [from the end]). See the examples below. (4) a. miínong 'I (man) am about to go' b. míina 'I (woman) am about to go' (5) a. hónna 'big' b. pońnaa 'many'. (C) Partial reduplication preposes the first two moras of the base word.
tone_statements.locator: p. 168, sec. 2.2 モーラ, item (B) with exx. (4)-(5)

audit.reasoning: The classification (predictable stress on the third mora from the end, first mora in bimoraic words; moras = vowels and coda /H Q N/; retraction off voiceless /H Q/; word domain; listed exceptions) rests on the standard and only reference grammar of Motuna (Onishi 1994 ANU thesis, 565 pp.), whose stress section is backed by the author's own F0 measurements. We hold the full open-access text and every part of the deciding quotation, the domain quotation and the exceptions footnote is present verbatim at the stated sections/pages. Glottolog 5.1 lists no better or later independent description: the 2011 LINCOM grammar is the thesis republished (OGFAUS 09), and Gasaway 1987 is a short unpublished SIL ms that Onishi cites and supersedes. Nothing downloaded contradicts the record; no reclassification or re-read is indicated. Files touched: held source above; listing pages
